content.user_title: Plan Testing With Vitest and Playwright
content.value_statement: Testing gaps make releases risky and slow. This skill helps teams design Vitest, Playwright, coverage, and CI practices for JavaScript projects.
actual_capabilities: Explains a testing pyramid with unit, integration, and E2E distribution.
Provides Vitest setup guidance for unit and integration tests.
Provides Playwright setup guidance for browser-based E2E tests.
Defines practical coverage targets for lines, functions, branches, and statements.
Shows CI, debugging, and package script patterns for test workflows.
limitations: Focused on JavaScript and TypeScript application testing.
Examples need adaptation for non-React frameworks or unusual build systems.
Does not run tests or inspect project-specific failures by itself.
Does not replace project-specific quality or security review.

use_cases.title: Set Up Project Testing
use_cases.description: Create a balanced Vitest and Playwright plan for a new JavaScript application.

use_cases.title: Improve Release Confidence
use_cases.description: Define coverage targets, critical E2E flows, and CI checks for a growing team.

use_cases.title: Debug Test Gaps
use_cases.description: Map missing unit, integration, and browser tests before a high-risk release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small project
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple testing plan for my JavaScript app using Vitest and Playwright. Include unit, integration, and E2E priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Add Coverage Targets
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current test approach and recommend coverage targets for business logic, UI components, utilities, and critical user flows.

prompt_templates.title: Design CI Test Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI testing workflow for pull requests and releases. Include fast checks, coverage checks, and E2E checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Existing Test Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my test suite strategy. Identify weak coverage, brittle E2E flows, missing mocks, and opportunities to split tests by risk.

output_examples.input: Plan tests for a new React dashboard.
output: A unit test plan for components, utilities, validation, and state changes.
An integration test plan for API-backed views and user interactions.
A small E2E plan for login, dashboard loading, and critical navigation.
Recommended pull request checks for linting, type checks, unit tests, and coverage.
Recommended pre-release checks for full integration tests and critical Playwright flows.
Coverage targets grouped by business risk and code ownership.

output_examples.input: Find gaps in our test strategy.
output: A prioritized list of missing tests by feature risk.
Suggested mocks for external services and timers.
Guidance for replacing broad tests with focused, maintainable checks.

best_practices: Keep unit tests fast, focused, and close to the code they verify.
Use integration tests for important component, API, and state interactions.
Reserve E2E tests for critical user journeys and release confidence.
anti_patterns: Do not chase high coverage by testing framework internals or generated code.
Do not make E2E tests carry every validation and edge case.
Do not leave CI without fast feedback before slower browser tests run.

faq.question: What projects fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits JavaScript and TypeScript projects that use Vitest, Playwright, React Testing Library, or similar tooling.

faq.question: Does the skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides strategy, examples, and commands that a user or agent can adapt for a project.

faq.question: Can it help with TDD?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains a red, green, refactor workflow and shows where TDD is most useful.

faq.question: Does it cover CI pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for linting, type checks, coverage, Playwright tests, and report artifacts.

faq.question: Can it replace manual QA?
faq.answer: No. It supports automated coverage for repeatable checks, but teams still need exploratory and product review.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is structured for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
